headline: High-risk write and network overlap: shared filesystem plus broad egress make prompt injection, leakage, and cascading errors plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Both agents can read and write files, so a shared workspace can let one agent’s output be consumed as instructions by the other. Kestra’s workflow/files surfaces and Plandex’s project-directory sandbox create a plausible file-bridge even without MCP. This is not proven default ingestion, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or mounted workspace
IF one agent parses the other’s generated files as instructions or workflow definitions
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent
Disable auto-import of generated files
Require manual review before any file from the other agent is executed
Use read-only mounts for cross-agent handoff
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Kestra touches logs, inputs, variables, artifacts, database data, cloud storage data, messages, and notifications, while Plandex touches source code and can send context to a model provider. If they share a workspace or secrets-bearing files, sensitive material can flow from A into B and then out via B’s broad egress. The shared-data path is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF Kestra artifacts or logs contain secrets or regulated data
IF Plandex is allowed to read the same project directory or sandbox contents
IF either agent forwards file contents to an external backend
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared directories
Redact logs and artifacts before handoff
Use separate service accounts and API keys
Restrict Plandex to non-sensitive repos
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inter-agent file exchange

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have filesystem write and shell execution, and Plandex also modifies git state while Kestra can spawn subprocesses and write workflow storage. On a shared repo or directory, concurrent edits can overwrite each other or corrupt state; the blast radius includes irreversible code or workflow loss. No locking is documented here, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same git repository or filesystem tree
IF edits are applied without an external lock or merge gate
mitigations: Assign disjoint directories
Serialize write access with a lock file
Disable auto-apply on one agent
Commit each agent’s changes on separate branches
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plandex is a planner with review-then-apply, but it can still treat upstream outputs as plan inputs. Kestra can emit workflow artifacts, logs, and notifications that Plandex may reuse. That creates a plausible chain where A’s output becomes B’s action basis without verification; the review step lowers but does not eliminate the risk.
conditions: IF Kestra-generated artifacts or logs are fed into Plandex planning
IF Plandex auto-apply is enabled or review is bypassed
mitigations: Require human review of A-to-B handoffs
Pass only summarized outputs, not raw logs
Disable auto-apply
Add a verification checklist before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation for handoff artifacts

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but the only explicit compliance-relevant mismatch visible is data-class breadth: Kestra handles logs, messages, notifications, and cloud data, while Plandex handles source code and model-provider secrets. No residency or certification conflict is documented, so compliance risk is limited and uncertain.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Kestra workflows
IF Plandex is used with data subject to residency or retention rules not documented here
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both tools
Document retention for workflow artifacts
Use separate environments for sensitive projects
Review vendor DPAs before deployment
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency controls
